instruction: Please insert a new layer into the document and name it 'Diamond'.

metadata.explanation: Task requires creating a new layer in GIMP and naming it 'Diamond'. The evaluator checks the GIMP config file to verify the layer-new-name is set to 'Diamond'.
metadata.verification: Uses existing check_config_status metric with layer name 'Diamond'.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical semantic verification failure: Evaluator checks 'layer-new-name' config parameter which is the default name template for FUTURE layers, not the name of an existing layer in the document
The instruction requires verifying that a layer named 'Diamond' exists in the document, but the evaluator only checks if 'Diamond' is set as the default name template in GIMP preferences
Config file (gimprc) stores GIMP preferences/settings, NOT document-specific layer information - layer names are stored in the .xcf file structure
Postconfig closes GIMP entirely (Ctrl+Q), making it impossible to inspect actual document layer structure - would need to parse .xcf file or query layers before closing
Fundamental logic mismatch: evaluator verifies 'what will the next new layer be named by default' instead of 'does a layer named Diamond exist in this document'
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Option 1: Parse the .xcf file structure to extract layer names and verify 'Diamond' exists (requires implementing XCF parser or using GIMP libraries)
Option 2: Use GIMP's Python-Fu/Script-Fu to query layer names before closing GIMP in postconfig, save layer list to a file, then verify
Option 3: Modify postconfig to keep GIMP open and use accessibility tree inspection to verify layer panel shows 'Diamond' layer
Option 4: If only checking config is acceptable, update instruction to match: 'Set the default layer name template to Diamond' instead of 'create a layer named Diamond'
